scope.paper_mechanism: MoMuSAM reuses previous momentum to choose a local perturbation before an orthogonalized momentum update; MuSAM uses an extra clean-gradient evaluation.
scope.miniature_comparison: A 150-step digits MLP comparing plain Muon-style updates, clean-gradient perturbations, and previous-momentum perturbations with shared batches and initialization. Approved admission scope: Compare the declared 150-step digits-MLP update rules under the documented architecture, approximate Newton-Schulz routine, shared initialization/batches and finite grid. No LLM result, exact polar factor or general optimizer guarantee.
preserved_assumptions: Previous momentum chooses the perturbation before the current gradient.
Zero momentum gives zero first-step perturbation.
Matrix momentum is orthogonalized approximately; all arms share splits, initialization, and minibatches.
simplifications: Tiny digits MLP instead of the source experimental models.
Five Newton-Schulz steps approximate a polar update; shape scaling and a cosine schedule are fixed.
Bias vectors are also perturbed and use momentum SGD; primary comparison fixes steps, not equal compute.
unsupported_claims: Replication of source benchmark accuracy, convergence theorems, or generalization guarantees.
Equal wall-clock or gradient-compute performance across all three methods.

evidence.finding: The perturbation uses the preceding momentum before the current perturbed gradient.
Block normalization uses zero perturbation for zero direction.
momusam takes one gradient at the momentum-perturbed point, then updates momentum and applies matrix orthogonalization. Bias treatment is an explicit extension.
